analysis.title: UBS Cash Trading - Main Themes 4th November
key_insights: Democrats swept control of both chambers of Congress. Tech-exposed markets opened sharply weaker, with Nasdaq futures down as much as 2.4% before trimming losses. Nasdaq and S&P were down about 50bps at time of writing, and EStoxx was down 50bps at the start, about 1% off the early lows.
The KOSPI rallied 4% off its lows back to unchanged. The desk reads this as market pricing having been more in line with odds markets on the midterm results.
The dollar was the cleaner expression of the result. It was broadly weaker, with USDJPY back below 158, CHF +0.5% and both EUR and GBP higher.

Gold rose about $50 to about $3,980/oz and UST 10-year yields eased 2bps to 4.94%. The desk says the market read the result as a sharp rebuke of Trump and a much narrower legislative runway, not a growth scare.
Earnings cushioned the AI complex. AMD, ANET, ALAB and SMCI all delivered beats with stronger outlooks, led by AI/data-center demand.
Company-specific moves: SWKS sold off on weak post-Qorvo guidance, FRSH fell on softer billings and a modest full-year trim, and VRNS beat but withheld guidance because of its pending acquisition.
China traded broadly higher, with CSI300 +3% and SHCOMP +1.9%. Semis were up 10% in the region as state measures to support markets continued to feed into prices.

Chinese retail appetite is cooling. The services gauge unexpectedly dipped for the first time since July, and October A-share new account openings fell 21.5% MoM and 35% YoY, despite the State Council's capital markets push in its report to the NPC.

Oil was steady with WTI about $96 as the US and Iran continued diplomacy despite limited American strikes. API showed a crude draw of 5.3m and distillates -1.2m, with builds in gasoline (+1.4m) and Cushing (+0.5m).

European cash equity flows finished balanced on Tuesday (50/50), with participation marginally below the HT YTD average. Industrials were the busiest sector at 26% of turnover and finished better for sale, with supply concentrated in electricals.

Banks were 21% of turnover and finished better bid on strong demand across Spanish and Dutch names. Healthcare (15%) saw two-way activity in large-cap pharma while MedTech was quiet. Energy (9%) saw supply as crude faded, and Tech saw marginal supply on muted volumes (4%).
